answer: An anchor is only trusted if two unrelated holders drove it. Each newcomer must plant an anchor alongside an existing one, with both holders countersigning the depth claim, and one anchor cannot serve two newcomers, so relaying it merges the claims into one berth. Every anchor is sampled like a raven caching food: the audit asks for the buried receipt, and a report contradicted on replay voids the whole canyon wall. The k-th anchor an operator drives costs k squared in bond, so n aliases pay near n cubed while still needing n distinct cosigners, and anchors cannot be sold or re-planted.
